intro: Searching for executor assistance near you usually means someone has died and you have been named as an executor, or you are helping an executor who is finding the role heavier than expected. You may be unsure what probate involves, what you are personally liable for, or how much of the work you can hand over. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK wills and probate specialist who can quote you directly, so you can decide how much help you want.
need_heading: What people searching for executor assistance usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for executor assistance want practical help with the paperwork and decisions that follow a death, without giving up control of the estate.
needs: You have been named as an executor in a will and want to understand what the role actually involves before you start.
The estate includes property, bank accounts or investments and you want help with valuations and the paperwork probate requires.
You are unsure about inheritance tax and want someone to explain what has to be reported and paid, and when.
You would like a professional to take on some or all of the work of applying for the grant of probate, while you stay informed.
You are acting alongside other executors, or you live far from the deceased, and the practical side of gathering information is proving difficult.
context_heading: Choosing help you can rely on
context: Writing a will is not a reserved legal activity in England and Wales, so some will writers are not regulated. Solicitors regulated by the SRA and chartered legal executives regulated by CILEx are insured and covered by the Legal Ombudsman, and many specialists are also members of STEP or Solicitors for the Elderly. Applying for a grant of probate on someone else's behalf for a fee is a reserved activity, so it is worth asking early how the person you speak to is regulated.

Because you searched for help near you, ask where the adviser is based and whether they work with estates in the right jurisdiction. Scotland has its own rules on succession and confirmation, so make sure your adviser practises there if the deceased lived in Scotland. It also helps to ask where original documents will be held and who will deal with your case day to day.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say where the deceased lived and where the estate's main assets are, so you are introduced to someone practising in the right place.
Explain whether you are the only executor or one of several, and whether all of you agree about getting help.
Mention whether there is a will and whether you have the original, or only a copy.
Describe the main assets, such as a house, savings, shares or a business, without listing exact values.
Say how much you want to hand over, from help with forms to full administration of the estate.
Mention any deadlines you are aware of, such as correspondence from HMRC or a bank, so the adviser can judge urgency.
questions: Are you regulated, and by which body, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Will you apply for the grant of probate on my behalf, and is that work covered by your regulation?
How will you keep me informed about progress, and who will be my main point of contact?
What will you need from me, and which decisions must I make as executor rather than you?
How do you charge for executor assistance, and what is included in your quote?
Where will the original will and other documents be stored while the estate is being dealt with?

faqs.q: Can I get help with only part of the executor work?
faqs.a: Yes. You can choose how much help you need, from a one-off conversation about the forms to handing over the whole administration. A specialist can explain which parts they can take on and which decisions stay with you as executor.

faqs.q: Can I step back as an executor if I no longer want the role?
faqs.a: Executors can step back before acting, but once you have started dealing with the estate it is more complicated. Speak to a specialist promptly if you are unsure, because the options depend on what you have already done.

faqs.q: Do I need to keep records of what I spend on the estate?
faqs.a: Yes. Keep receipts for expenses, as they may need to be accounted for when the estate is finalised. A specialist can tell you which costs can properly be met from the estate.

faqs.q: Does it matter where the professional is based if I want help near me?
faqs.a: It can, because the estate is usually dealt with where the deceased lived and where the assets are. Ask about jurisdiction as well as location, particularly if the deceased lived in Scotland, which has its own rules on succession and confirmation.
